August 2021Elk Falls Overlook, Staunton State Park, Colorado

Elk Falls Overlook

memories below

Granite Afternoon

A dome of gray granite looks down on Elk Falls Pond, and the pond looks right back. I came to Staunton State Park on a Sunday afternoon in August, not far from home, with the mountain bike along for the ride. The pond sits in a conifer valley, small and dark and calm, with a wooden fence and a few wildflowers along the shore. White cumulus piled up over the ridge and doubled itself in the water. The brown sign by the shore lays out the rules: fishing license required, no swimming, no boats, rafts or other floating devices. Admiring it from the bank is the whole idea.

The overlook is where the afternoon opened up. From a bare ledge of warm granite the ground drops away into a canyon of pink and orange spires and fins, thick with conifers. Elk Falls itself, I think, is the thin white thread near the bottom, so far down that it is easy to miss. Squint toward the bottom right of the shots below and you can find it. The pink stone is ancient granite that cooled slowly deep underground and was uncovered as everything above it wore away. Heavy gray clouds rolled across the ridges while a warm haze stacked the distance into soft layers, and the light slid from silver toward gold.

On the way out I stopped at the pond one more time. The light had flattened and the water had gone dark and glassy, so the bike got its portraits, once beside the sign and once on the rocks by the shore. Next to rock that old, a mountain bike looks like a toy.
